$comment: The import-line shapes a promise is read by, as data, so a language is added here and not in code. `names`: the line binds named exports (group 1 the list, group 2 the module word); `whole`: it binds the module itself (group 1 the name, group 2 the module word). `entries`: the file stems that make a folder a module (its other files are its own). A shape is read wherever it stands in a line (a sentence, backticks), never glued to a name before it; the whole statement is the shape, a bare module word is none. A language whose import line has none of these shapes gives no promise: nothing is said, never a false contract. core/promise.cjs is the one reader. `store`: DecisionBook's own ear, the statements a prompt held, one row each ({ statement, module, names, session, at }, never another word of the prompt), in the person's home folder for this repository (base/here: never inside the repository, so no `git add` can take a person's words); `cap.kept` rows, the oldest goes.
